title: The pluperfect: what had already happened

sections.content: You know the pluperfect (*pluscuamperfecto*) from B1 Unit 1: *había* + past participle puts one event before another event in the past. It is the right tool for a story with a turning point, such as the fall of the Somoza regime: what had already happened before that moment.

items.spanish: Cuando cayó Somoza, la familia había gobernado más de cuarenta años.
items.english: When Somoza fell, the family had ruled for more than forty years.

items.spanish: Sandino había luchado contra las tropas de Estados Unidos.
items.english: Sandino had fought against US troops.

items.spanish: Cuando los sandinistas tomaron el poder, el último Somoza ya había huido del país.
items.english: When the Sandinistas took power, the last Somoza had already fled the country.

items.spanish: Los jóvenes habían fundado el FSLN en 1961, muchos años antes.
items.english: The young people had founded the FSLN in 1961, many years earlier.

sections.content: Put the later event in the *indefinido* (*cayó*, *tomaron*) and the earlier one in the pluperfect (*había gobernado*, *había huido*). *Ya* before *había* stresses "already". The participle never changes: *había gobernado*, *habían fundado*.
